To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have measured the top mass using two variables with minimal jet energy scale dependence, the mean decay length of the b-tagged jets and the transverse momentum distribution of the lepton.
we have made three measurements of the mass of the top quarks using two variables, L2d and LepPt, with minimal sensitivity to the jet energy scale.

(i) we have developed a method to determine the top quark's mass that is largely independent of the jet energy scale; (ii) using this method we measure the top quark to have a mass of (176 ± 6 (stat) ± 3 (syst)) GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mass of the top quarks.
the measurement of the top mass using quantities that are less susceptible to the uncertainty in the jet energy scale than the usual methods.
the measurement of the top quarks mass using quantities with minimal dependance on the jet energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the top quark is heavy, and the mass is consistent with the standard model prediction.
these results are the most accurate top mass measurements to date, with the exception of the Tevatron CDF top mass measurement from 2009, which used a different technique.

the top mass measurement using L2d, LepPt and both variables simultaneously are all consistent with the world average top mass and the world average top quark mass measurement using the jet energy scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the top quark is a massive particle with a mass between 172 GeV/c2 to 178 GeV/c2, and the mass is measured to be 173.6 GeV/c2 with a precision of 1.0%.
the top mass measurement in the lepton + jets channel using the LepPt method is the most precise of the three measurements.
we have measured the top quark using a method that is independent of the jet energy scale, and we find a top mass consistent with the world average.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet energy scale is not a limiting factor in measuring the top mass.
the top mass can be measured with a precision comparable to that achieved in the electron channel with the L2d method and with the LepPt method.
